notes: GSC latest available day advanced to 2026-09-18, so the 28-day window moved to 2026-08-22..2026-09-18 (was 2026-08-20..2026-09-16 on the 2026-09-19 snapshot).
Aggregation method validated: recomputing the previous run's window (2026-08-20..2026-09-16) from today's 90-day daily table reproduces 122 clicks / 5,282 impressions / 2.31% / position 40.0 exactly.

GSC clicks 119 vs 166 (-28.3%) and impressions 4,955 vs 6,398 (-22.6%). This is again largely a sliding-window artefact: the comparison window now runs 2026-07-25..2026-08-21 and contains the strongest days of the whole 90-day series (13 Aug = 16 clicks / 322 impressions, 4 Aug = 12 / 267, 5 Aug = 10 / 306). Those days are outside the current window. It is not a collapse.

The genuine, non-artefact signal this run is the impression tail thinning while position improves sharply. 16-18 Sep carry only 100 / 75 / 83 impressions against a 150-250 norm, yet average position on those days is 21.8 / 19.3 / 19.7 - the three best daily positions in the entire 90-day series (late August sat at 44-57). 16 Sep was also 100 impressions on the 2026-09-19 scan, so it has settled; 17-18 Sep are the two newest days and may still be revised up. Reading: Google is dropping deep long-tail impressions (positions 50-85) and keeping the ones that rank well.
18 Sep returned 6 clicks from 83 impressions - a 7.2% CTR, the highest single-day CTR of the 28-day window.
2026-09-14 still reports 0 clicks against 164 impressions, now unchanged across five consecutive scans. Confirmed as a genuine zero-click day.

Weekly view: the rolling week 2026-09-12..2026-09-18 gives 21 clicks / 883 impressions / 2.38% / position 29.6, against 37 / 1,322 / 2.80% / 33.5 the week before. Clicks -43.2% and impressions -33.2% - but three of the seven days are the thin 16-18 Sep tail described above, and position is the best of the four weeks.

GA4 sessions 776 vs 1,280 (-39.4%). Same cause as the last four runs: the anomalous 18 Aug Direct spike still sits inside the comparison window 2026-07-28..2026-08-24 and is outside the current window. Direct alone fell 748 -> 324, i.e. 424 of the 504-session gap.

GA4 key events fell to 15 (from 45 in the comparison period), split 8 Organic Search / 5 Direct / 2 Paid Search. Organic's share of key events is 53.3%. The organic sessions vs organic key events gap (-23.0% vs -75.8%) is still far too wide to explain with traffic, and the key-event / contact-form tracking check flagged on nine previous scans has still not been done.
Paid Search is the only channel growing on sessions: 163 vs 86 (+89.5%), but it produced 2 key events at a 0.61% session key-event rate.
/technology holds second place on GA4 views at 200 (+166.7% period on period) and is now well ahead of /services. /contact-us views fell to 26 (-70.8%) but still carry 9 of the 15 key events.
